As a beginner runner training for a marathon, it's essential to fuel your body with the right foods to optimize your performance and recovery. According to the Athletes Diet framework [athletes_diet_8.md], a balanced meal plan should include protein in every meal, high-quality carbohydrates for training days, and mindful fats for energy.

For a marathon, you'll want to focus on complex carbohydrates, such as whole grains, fruits, and vegetables, which provide sustained energy and support muscle function. Good sources of complex carbohydrates include sweet potatoes, brown rice, and whole-grain bread.

In addition to complex carbohydrates, include lean protein sources, such as lean meats, fish, eggs, dairy, or plant-based options like beans, lentils, and tofu, to support muscle repair and growth. Aim for a balanced meal with a mix of protein and complex carbohydrates 1-3 hours before your marathon.

Some examples of pre-marathon meals include:

* Oatmeal with banana, almond butter, and a splash of low-fat milk
* Whole-grain toast with avocado, eggs, and a sprinkle of salt
* Grilled chicken or fish with quinoa, roasted vegetables, and a side salad

Remember to stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water and electrolyte-rich fluids, such as sports drinks or coconut water, to help replace lost electrolytes and prevent dehydration [post_run_recovery_2.md].

It's also essential to listen to your body and experiment with different foods to find what works best for you. Avoid new or unfamiliar foods on the day of the marathon to minimize the risk of digestive discomfort.

Lastly, don't forget to refuel with a balanced meal or snack within 30-60 minutes after the marathon to support muscle recovery and replenish energy stores [post_run_recovery_2.md].

Remember to consult with a sports dietitian or a healthcare professional for personalized nutrition advice.
